title: Matyó embroidery
summary: In and around Mezőkövesd in northern Hungary, embroiderers work large, bold flowers in padded satin stitch and stem stitch. Roses, tulips and buds in scarlet, blue, green and gold stand out on black or white cloth and trim blouses, aprons and household linen.
howToPlay: Pick a silk colour from the hanks and a flower shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the cloth to stitch that shape there; it is mirrored across and down.
Copy the bouquet shown on the chart, then press Check.
rules: The bouquet is mirrored left to right and top to bottom, so every shape you stitch is also stitched on its partner squares.
A square counts only when its shape and its silk colour both match the bouquet you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Matyó embroidery grew up in the town of Mezőkövesd and nearby villages in northern Hungary, where women embroidered their own costume and household linen. The embroidery was recognised internationally as living heritage in 2012.
